decision: installed Go 1.27.3, the current stable release
why: the task asks for current stable Go, verified rather than assumed
evidence: go.dev/dl/?mode=json lists go1.27.3 and go1.26.10 as stable

decision: installed the real Cursor CLI and probed agent acp before designing
why: the ACP backend is the riskiest unknown, so measure it first
result: initialize works logged out; session/new returns -32000 Authentication required

decision: use github.com/coder/acp-go-sdk v0.13.5 for the ACP backend
why: a probe program using the SDK client completed initialize against the real agent acp and decoded its error as acp.RequestError
result: SDK interoperates for the handshake; prompt turns stay unverified without login

decision: add a timeout around the ACP authenticate call
why: authenticate with cursor_login never replied when logged out
evidence: probe sent authenticate, no reply within 12s
result: open item for real CLI: behavior when logged in

decision: print backend gets its chat id from agent create-chat
why: create-chat printed a UUID without login, so the id is known before the first turn like an ACP session id
result: verified logged out; agent -p exits 1 with an auth error when logged out

decision: one prompt queue in the lifecycle holds the launch prompt and later follow-ups
why: the first prompt and follow-ups follow the same send-next rule, so there is one code path instead of two

decision: close the agent process when a run finishes and resume with session/load on follow-up
why: idle agent processes cost memory per finished run, and a daemon restart needs the resume path anyway, so one path covers both
evidence: lifecycle FollowUp on Finished returns StartBackend{Resume: true}
result: open item: session/load unverified on the real CLI

decision: pending permissions are a FIFO list, not a single slot
why: an agent can request permissions for parallel tool calls; a single slot would lose one

decision: stop keeps the clb/<id> branch and deletes only the worktree directory
why: commits the agent made survive stop; only uncommitted changes are discarded

decision: stop on a failed run keeps the failed state and only retries worktree cleanup
why: overwriting failed with stopped hides why the run ended; repeating stop must converge
evidence: lifecycle_test.go stop on a failed run keeps the failure

decision: skip the architect arena for this design
why: the user fixed the architecture in twelve decisions; the remaining choices are internal shapes I sketched as typed contracts, and a second design bakeoff over settled decisions adds cost without new options

decision: no store interface in the daemon; tests use the real SQLite store
why: the user's rule is interfaces only where tests need fakes; modernc SQLite runs in-process in a temp dir, so no test needs a store fake
a test that survives a broken transition proves nothing
result: 3 killed at first; the survivor led to a new row, then killed

decision: split the build into three workers on separate worktrees: adapters, backends with the fake agent, and daemon with ipc, cli, and E2E
why: the packages touch disjoint files, so the only shared write is go.mod, which go mod tidy resolves at merge

decision: picked models by difficulty: grok-4.7-high for the adapters, claude-opus-5-5-xhigh for the ACP backend, claude-opus-5-5-max for the daemon
why: the daemon actor and session cleanup are the subtlest concurrency in the project; the adapters are routine

decision: session generation counter in the daemon actor
why: after stop, finish, and a resumed follow-up, a late TurnEnded from the old agent process must not end the new turn; the lifecycle alone cannot tell old from new
